headline: No documented pairwise interaction; prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are blocked by absent shared channels and no write/network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable collection with no I/O surfaces; Agent B cannot read files, use MCP, or accept clipboard/stdin. With no shared channel, there is no plausible default prompt-injection bridge between them.
conditions: IF either agent is wrapped by an external orchestrator that copies outputs into the other agent's prompt, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or message queue.
Disable any wrapper that forwards one agent's text into the other's prompt.
Require manual review before copying outputs between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent has network egress, and B cannot read files or stdout/stderr. A touches no data classes, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow from A to B or out to a third party.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes sensitive content into B, leakage risk would come from that external action, not the documented pair.
mitigations: Do not paste sensitive content between the agents.
Keep network egress disabled on both agents.
Use separate workspaces and accounts for any surrounding tooling.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and exposes no write or git capabilities; B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable surface, so capability conflict is provably blocked.
conditions: IF an external system grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would arise outside the current profiles.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same environment.
Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace.
Do not grant git or filesystem write permissions to either agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A does not produce operational outputs and B is a customer-support agent with no documented action-taking authority. Since B also lacks file, shell, and browser execution, there is no default path for A's output to cascade into harmful downstream actions.
conditions: IF an orchestrator treats A's text as authoritative instructions for another system, cascading error could occur through that external integration.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action.
Require human approval for any action derived from model text.
Do not connect A's outputs directly to automation.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched by either agent, and both profiles show no secrets handled or residency-sensitive flows. With no documented regulated-data processing, there is no compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, a separate compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document any future data-class changes before deployment.
Re-run compliance review if residency or retention settings change.
